This indicates a possible pathway where Selgantolimod may influence the activity of Magnesium levulinate, which then affects the Serum amyloid P-component. The high scores in both paths (0.7334) suggest a strong predictive relationship, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains unclear. The evidence supports a potential regulatory or functional link between Selgantolimod and Serum amyloid P-component, but further experimental validation is needed to confirm the nature of this relationship.
